metaTitle: The Fatty Crab Case Study: 46M+ Views | Button Up Media
metaDescription: How Button Up Media grew The Fatty Crab in Doral to 46M+ video views and 350K+ followers across Instagram, Facebook and TikTok with short video.
ldHeadline: The Fatty Crab: 46M+ social video views for a Doral seafood boil restaurant
answer: We run social media for The Fatty Crab, a Cajun seafood boil spot in Doral. Short videos built around the food reached 46M+ views on Instagram, Facebook and TikTok.

hero.alt: A seafood boil poured out at The Fatty Crab, from a Reel we made with 2.6M views

metrics.label: Video views
metrics.meaning: Instagram Reels 34.3M, Facebook 9.1M and TikTok 2.7M, measured in Sprout Social from January 2022 to November 2026.

metrics.label: Followers
metrics.meaning: Facebook 182K, Instagram 155K and TikTok 16K. That's an audience The Fatty Crab can post to without paying for ads.

metrics.label: Instagram engagement rate
metrics.meaning: This is how often people who see a post like, comment on or share it. Across all three platforms, the rate is 5.5%.

paragraphs: The feed was mostly static posts on an inconsistent schedule.
We thought a Cajun seafood boil would come across much better on video than in an occasional photo.

items.title: Plan around four content pillars
items.bodyHtml: We planned posts around four content pillars: the food, the experience, the people and the culture.

items.title: Build video templates
items.bodyHtml: We created short video formats we could reuse, so shooting and editing stayed quick.

items.title: Post when the audience is online
items.bodyHtml: We timed posts on Instagram and Facebook for when their followers are most active.

items.title: Write captions that lead to a visit
items.bodyHtml: We wrote every hook, caption and call to action to get people to book a table or come in.

items.title: Post a delivery Reel at dinnertime
items.bodyHtml: We posted one organic Reel showing orders being packed, with an “Order on Uber Eats” call to action, during peak delivery hours. It brought in Uber Eats orders without any ad spend.

items.title: Work with a local food creator
items.bodyHtml: From July 2023 to March 2024 we worked with a food creator who has a strong following in Miami and South Florida. We planned the videos together around the signature dishes, the dining room and the staff. We posted them on Instagram and TikTok at the times people were most likely to find them, then reshared them, featured them in Stories and answered comments.

items.title: Reels past 1 million views on Instagram
items.body: Of the 393 Reels on @thefattycrab, 11 have passed a million views, and the top two have 2.6M each. With that many Reels past a million, the results have held up across many videos.

items.title: top Reels promote a specific offer
items.body: They're the Doral brunch deal, the all-you-can-eat New Orleans brunch and the BOGO shrimp boils on Uber Eats. A clear offer gives people a reason to come in soon.

items.title: comments on one Reel, many of them people tagging friends
items.body: The Reel “Your first @ owes you a seafood boil” asks viewers to tag someone. Each tag shows the video to another person, which helped it reach 2.6M views.

items.title: views on a creator-led Reel
items.body: During our influencer campaign, local food creators hosted the New Orleans brunch Reel, which also put The Fatty Crab in front of their followers.

points: The influencer campaign brought in a lot of new followers, and more guests mentioned the creator's videos when they came in.
